question: What is the primary focus of Quality Assurance in nursing?

options.A: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors
options.B: Systematically monitoring and improving patient care standards
options.C: Reducing the salaries of healthcare workers to cut hospital costs
options.D: Increasing the number of patient admissions per day

explanation: Quality assurance focuses on systematically evaluating and improving clinical processes and patient care standards rather than punishing staff. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following bodies sets professional standards and regulatory frameworks for nursing in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) is the regulatory body responsible for setting professional standards for nursing in Nigeria. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is a primary objective of Quality Assurance in nursing related to clinical errors?

options.A: To hide errors from hospital management
options.B: To minimize clinical errors and enhance patient safety
options.C: To document errors without taking corrective action
options.D: To blame individual nurses for systemic failures

explanation: A major objective of QA is to minimize clinical errors like medication mistakes and falls, thereby enhancing overall patient safety. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h2)

question: How does Quality Assurance impact patient satisfaction?

options.A: By reducing the time nurses spend communicating with patients
options.B: By fostering therapeutic relationships and respecting patient dignity
options.C: By eliminating the need for patient feedback
options.D: By focusing solely on hospital profitability

explanation: QA aims to boost patient satisfaction by fostering therapeutic nurse-patient relationships, effective communication, and respecting patient dignity. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h2)

question: In the Donabedian model of healthcare quality, what does 'process' refer to?

options.A: The physical hospital building and equipment
options.B: The actual delivery of care and nursing interventions
options.C: The financial budget of the hospital
options.D: The final recovery rate of the patient

explanation: Process encompasses the actual delivery of care, including nursing assessments, interventions, and adherence to established clinical protocols. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h3)

question: What are the four stages of the Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycle?
explanation: The PDSA cycle stands for Plan, Do, Study, Act, serving as an iterative framework for carrying out continuous quality improvement. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a clinical audit in nursing?

options.A: To calculate the monthly salaries of nursing personnel
options.B: To review nursing documentation and records against established criteria
options.C: To punish nurses who write illegible notes
options.D: To order new medical supplies for the ward

explanation: Clinical audits involve systematically reviewing nursing documentation and patient records against predetermined criteria to evaluate care quality. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why are incident reports valuable in healthcare quality assurance?

options.A: They provide data on adverse events and near misses for root cause analysis
options.B: They serve as legal documents to terminate employment immediately
options.C: They replace the need for patient satisfaction surveys
options.D: They track the daily attendance of ward nurses

explanation: Incident reports provide critical data on adverse events and near misses, allowing teams to analyze root causes and prevent future occurrences. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned to drive Quality Assurance in healthcare facilities?

options.A: They make all hospital financial and budgetary decisions
options.B: They maintain continuous, 24-hour contact with hospitalized patients
options.C: They are solely responsible for writing national health policies
options.D: They manage the hospital pharmacy inventory

explanation: Nurses maintain continuous 24-hour contact with patients, making them uniquely positioned to observe patient status and clinical safety hazards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a key bedside responsibility of nurses regarding quality improvement protocols?

options.B: Translating broad quality goals into rigorous daily bedside practices
options.C: Delegating all clinical documentation to non-medical staff
options.D: Avoiding participation in hospital quality committees

explanation: Nurses act as change agents by translating broad organizational quality goals into rigorous daily bedside practices like infection control bundles. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a major human resource challenge affecting Quality Assurance in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: An overwhelming surplus of highly specialized nurses
options.B: Severe nurse-to-patient ratios and high workloads due to brain drain
options.C: Nurses refusing to work night shifts
options.D: Mandatory retirement age set too low

explanation: Severe nurse-to-patient ratios and the migration of skilled nurses (brain drain) create high workloads, leaving little time for QA activities. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h6)

question: How does paper-based record-keeping negatively impact healthcare quality assurance in Nigeria?

options.A: It makes data collection instantaneous and foolproof
options.B: It is prone to loss, damage, and illegibility, hindering accurate measurement
options.C: It automatically generates advanced statistical trend charts
options.D: It eliminates the need for clinical audits

explanation: Paper-based records are frequently prone to loss, damage, and illegibility, which creates barriers to accurate data collection and quality measurement. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary benefit of fostering a 'just culture' in clinical practice?

options.A: It ensures that every staff member who makes an error is immediately dismissed
options.B: It views errors as learning opportunities, encouraging transparent incident reporting
options.C: It eliminates the need for clinical supervision and audits
options.D: It focuses exclusively on financial cost-cutting measures

explanation: A just culture views errors as learning opportunities rather than reasons for victimization, which encourages transparent reporting and safety improvements. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why is interprofessional collaboration important for sustaining quality improvement?

options.A: It allows nurses to take over the responsibilities of all other hospital departments
options.B: It helps streamline clinical pathways and eliminate inter-departmental bottlenecks
options.C: It prevents nurses from participating in hospital management meetings
options.D: It replaces the need for continuous professional education

explanation: Collaboration among nurses, doctors, pharmacists, and administrators streamlines clinical pathways and removes bottlenecks that affect patient care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h7)
